CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left-sided lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with left-sided lower back pain. He reports having back surgery in November 2020 for a microdiscectomy due to a herniated disk that wrapped around his spinal thecal sac. He experienced severe nerve pain down his leg following the surgery and was treated with high-dose gabapentin, which was difficult to discontinue. Currently, he experiences left-sided lower back pain that varies day to day and sometimes involves the right side. Pain is worse with bending over and occurs randomly. Stretching provides relief. He is currently taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily for pain management. He denies current nerve pain down his legs. Pain is present with weightbearing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current nerve pain down legs. No other problems discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back surgery (microdiscectomy) in November 2020.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient standing and able to ambulate. Spine: No pain with forward flexion or extension. Pain present with weightbearing while standing. Pain with palpation to left side around L5. No pain with palpation to right side. Lower extremities: Dorsiflexion normal bilaterally. Normal lower extremity strength with ability to push against examiner's hands. No pain down legs bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures. Previous surgical site shows appropriate healing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left-sided lower back pain, likely secondary to muscle pull from spinal misalignment post-microdiscectomy. Plan: (1) Physical therapy referral; (2) Discontinue ibuprofen and start meloxicam; (3) Referral to pain management for discussion of pain management strategies and potential use of non-narcotic alternatives; (4) Demerol prescribed.
